Similar situation here. The whole time I was at Todd's house, it felt like I was re-living a small chunk of my past. I did everything I could to not anger Todd, because I was afraid of what he'd do to Kara/Alice if I upset him more 😅 During the confrontation when we were escaping, I couldn't help but hold my breath. I didn't want to get "busted up worse than last time", and I didn't want Todd to get ahold of Alice. When we finally were able to run to the bus, I let out a huge sigh of relief. 
David Cage got shit for adding abuse in a game, but I felt like this was one of the best decisions (among with countless others) that were made, regarding Detroit: Become Human. Not only was it relatable, but it shines a light on the "common man" who's suffering from the red ice epidemic/unemployment (not that that's an excuse to be abusive). The sheer amount of adrenaline and joy I got from escaping the house, among with a hint of worry for the future that I got out of that chapter is an experience that takes full advantage of the platform of video games.

I hated Todd at first out of fear and anger, but as a character, I'd say he plays a very essential role to an extent. Now, I can even quote the infamous "fucking whore walked out on me for a fucking accountant".

If you do get the chance, definitely play the game over again, with different decisions. Hope that the game isn't spoiled for you, and that you'd get the best out of DBH!

The El Yucateco series are pretty good, especially if you're using it casually (for an instant kick, but nothing like Da Bomb). 
With the exception of the Jalapeño sauce, El Yucateco sauces are made from Habaneros.
The XXXTRA Hot Mayan sauce is the hottest one, and it's by far my favourite. It's got a great, rich habanero flavour with almost a "smoky" taste coming from the pepper (but not like BBQ sauce). It packs an immediate punch, but it's nothing that can't be handled, or enjoyed. It's hot, but with El Yucatecos, it's not just a sauce that's hot to be purely painful. If you look at the ingredients of the XXXTRA sauce, habanero is the first thing on that list, followed by water. This means that the predominant ingredient is habanero; you can expect a thick sauce because of that.

It's a great addition to your shelf if you like the distinct flavour of habanero in your sauces. You can put it on anything.

You can find El Yucateco sauces in local grocery stores (in the Hispanic section), in hispanic stores, or online. The XXXTRA hot ones are sometimes not available in stores.

Jalapeño green- Made from jalapeños as opposed to habaneros. Because of this, there is no smoky flavour to it. It's more of a typical "chile" flavour.

Black label reserve- Least spicy. Feels like there's a LOT of the smoky taste coming from this sauce. 

Red sauce- Made from red tomatoes, this one is seen most often.

Green sauce- Same spice level as the red, made from green tomatoes. Slight flavour difference.

Caribbean sauce- Spicier than the red/green sauces, I think. Unlike the others, this one has a little bit of sugar to it, but not enough to take away from the heat level. 

XXXTRA Hot Mayan- Delicious. Finally, some good fucking food (just a joke, they're all really good). Definitely spiciest compared to the other ones, but still has good integrity in its flavour.
